doc.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014

chapter: Writing, criticism and the jazz business
title: Starting out as a jazz writer
summary: Thomas describes his first article for Urban Profile in 1989, staff work at the City Sun and later columns, and the difficulty of making a living freelancing.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: But you found a way to work in jazz as a writer and a producer. How did that sort of evolve?

Well let’s see. Well the writer is first. Back in 1989 there was a publication called Urban Profile that was started by Keith Clinkscales and Leonard Burnett — their first magazine. They later went on to jointly put out five magazines, Savoy Magazine, they both have very successful careers. Len Burnett is now I think the chief revenue officer — they create these titles — for Uptown Magazine, which is based in Harlem but that covers goings on for I’d say the upper middle class black society, the black community in major cities — you know, Atlanta, Chicago, New York and like that. So for this publication I wrote an article and it was an advocacy piece — why black folks need to support jazz. So that was my very first professional piece. And I freelanced. Actually in ’91 I began as a staff writer at the City Sun, which was a black-owned newspaper in Brooklyn that was a very good newspaper, you know, defunct after a few years. But I mean I’ve written for the Guardian Observer; for various online publications from “Salon” to “Root,” Africana.com when it was around, “Black World Today”; and in print publications, I was a New York Daily News jazz columnist for a few years; Savoy Magazine I wrote for, American Legacy magazine I did some writing for, and a number of others. So the writing has been I guess the longest thing, and considering the way the internet has upended publishing and various industries, not just publishing but every industry really. Certainly being a journalist, unless you are one of the holders of a coveted staff position © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
at a really well-healed publication, it’s really hard to make a living at free-lance writing. So I’ve always had to supplement, you know, teaching and doing other things.
